translations.idiomatic: On the jihai new moon in the seventh month palace commander Wang Chao became supreme commander on the Xia, Sui, Lin, and Fu frontier.

sentences.zh: 庚子，詔作壽寧觀成。

translations.literal: On gengzi, an edict announced completion of the Shouning Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi he proclaimed the Shouning Abbey finished.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，給事中、參知政事寇準罷守本官。

translations.literal: On bingyin, Supervising Censor and Participant in Governance Kou Zhun was dismissed to his original post.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Vice Councilor Kou Zhun was removed from the council and returned to his remonstrance post.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，蠲峽路諸州民去年逋租。

translations.literal: On wuchen, last year's overdue rent for the people of the Gorges Route prefectures was remitted.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen he canceled the previous year's back taxes in the gorges prefectures.

sentences.zh: 是月，汴水決穀熟縣，許、宿、齊三州蝗抱草死。

translations.literal: That month the Bian River broke its banks at Gusou county; in Xu, Su, and Qi prefectures locusts clung to grass and died.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Bian Canal burst at Gusou, while in Xu, Su, and Qi locusts starved clinging to the grass.

sentences.zh: 閏月庚寅，詔江、浙、福建民負人錢沒入男女者還其家，敢匿者有罪。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on gengyin, an edict ordered that in Jiang, Zhe, and Fujian, where people's debts had led to the confiscation of sons and daughters, the children were returned to their families; whoever concealed them was guilty.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin in the intercalary month he decreed that children seized in Jiang, Zhe, and Fujian for debt be returned home, on pain of punishment for anyone who hid them.

sentences.zh: 八月辛丑，密州言蝗不為災。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on xinchou, Mi prefecture reported that locusts did no harm.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou in the eighth month Mizhou reported locusts that caused no damage.

sentences.zh: 冬十月己未，詔以池州新鑄錢監為永豐監。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jiwei, an edict made the new coin foundry of Chizhou the Yongfeng Mint.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei in the tenth month he designated Chizhou's new mint as the Yongfeng Mint.

sentences.zh: 十一月丁卯朔，增司天新曆為一百二十甲子。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on dingmao the new moon, the Directorate of Astronomy's new calendar was extended to one hundred twenty sexagenary cycles.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingmao new moon in the eleventh month the Astronomical Bureau's calendar was lengthened to one hundred twenty sexagenary cycles.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，置簽署提點樞密、宣徽院諸房公事。

translations.literal: On wuyin, the post of Signing and Reviewing Commissioner for the Bureau of Military Affairs and Northern and Southern Palace Secretariat bureaus was established.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin he created the office of signing commissioner to review paperwork for military affairs and the palace secretariats.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，許州群盜劫郾城縣居民，巡檢李昌習鬬死，都巡檢使王正襲擊之，獲賊首宋斌及餘黨，皆斬於市。

translations.literal: On xinmao, bandits in Xu prefecture raided the residents of Yancheng county; patrol inspector Li Changxi died fighting; chief patrol inspector Wang Zheng made a surprise attack, captured the bandit leader Song Bin and the rest of the party, and all were beheaded in the market.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Xu bandits plundered Yancheng county; patrol inspector Li Changxi was killed in the fight, but chief inspector Wang Zheng stormed them, seized leader Song Bin and his gang, and had them all beheaded.

sentences.zh: 甲午，禁淮南通行鹽稅。

translations.literal: On jiawu, the Huainan transit salt tax was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu he banned the Huainan salt transit levy.

sentences.zh: 十二月，命宰相以下百官詣諸寺觀禱雪。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, chief ministers and all officials down were ordered to pray for snow at temples and abbeys.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he sent the chief ministers and the entire bureaucracy to temples and abbeys to pray for snow.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，雨雪。

translations.literal: On jiayin, rain and snow.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin rain turned to snow.

sentences.zh: 大有年。

translations.literal: There was a great harvest.
translations.idiomatic: The year brought a bumper harvest.

sentences.zh: 是歲，處州稻再熟。

translations.literal: That year, rice in Chuzhou ripened twice.
translations.idiomatic: That year Chuzhou saw a second rice crop.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月丙子，以戶部侍郎溫仲舒、禮部侍郎王化基並參知政事，給事中李惟清同知樞密院事，參知政事張洎罷為刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month of the third year, on bingzi, Vice Director of Revenue Wen Zhongshu and Vice Director of Rites Wang Huaji were both made Participants in Governance; Supervising Censor Li Weiqing was made Associate Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs; Participant in Governance Zhang Ji was dismissed to Vice Director of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi in the first month of Zhidao 3 Revenue Vice Minister Wen Zhongshu and Rites Vice Minister Wang Huaji joined the council; Supervising Censor Li Weiqing became associate director of military affairs; Vice Councilor Zhang Ji was sent to the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，孝章皇后陪葬永昌陵。

translations.literal: On yiyou, Empress Xiaozhang was buried with the Founding Ancestor at Yongchang Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou Empress Xiaozhang was interred beside Taizu at Yongchang Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，以侍衛馬步軍都虞候傅潛為延州路都部署，殿前都虞候王昭遠為靈州路都部署。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Palace Cavalry and Foot chief commandant Fu Qian was made overall deployment commander of the Yanzhou route, and Palace Front chief commandant Wang Zhaoyuan was made overall deployment commander of the Lingzhou route.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Fu Qian, chief commandant of the palace horse and foot guards, took the Yanzhou command, and Wang Zhaoyuan the Lingzhou command.

sentences.zh: 二月丙申朔，靈州行營破李繼遷。

translations.literal: In the second month, on bingshen the new moon, the Lingzhou field headquarters defeated Li Jiqian.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen new moon in the second month the Lingzhou expedition routed Li Jiqian.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，帝不豫。

translations.literal: On xinchou, the Emperor was unwell.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou Taizong fell ill.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，降京畿死罪囚，流以下釋之。

translations.literal: On jiachen, capital death sentences were reduced, and exile and below were released.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen he commuted capital sentences in the capital and freed those below exile.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，大食、賓同隴國並來貢。

translations.literal: On renxu, Dashi and Bintonglong states both sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu the Abbasid caliphate and Bintonglong both sent tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 三月丁卯，占城國來貢。

translations.literal: In the third month, on dingmao, Champa sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao in the third month Champa presented tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，不視朝。

translations.literal: On renchen, he did not hold court.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen he ceased to hold audience.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，追班于萬歲殿，宣詔令皇太子柩前即位。

translations.literal: On guisi, he returned to court at Wansui Hall, proclaimed an edict ordering the Crown Prince to ascend the throne before the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi he appeared once more at Wansui Hall, issued the edict, and had the crown prince succeed him at the bier.

sentences.zh: 是日崩，年五十九。

translations.literal: That day he died, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died that same day, at fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 在位二十二年，殯于殿之西階。

translations.literal: He reigned twenty-two years and was encoffined on the western steps of the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-two years on the throne; his body lay in state on the hall's western steps.

sentences.zh: 群臣上尊諡曰神功聖德文武皇帝，廟號太宗。

translations.literal: The hundred officials submitted the posthumous title Emperor of Divine Merit, Sagely Virtue, Civil and Military Excellence, and the temple name Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: The court gave him the posthumous title Emperor of Divine Merit, Sagely Virtue, Civil and Military Excellence, and the temple name Taizong.

sentences.zh: 十月己酉，葬永熙陵。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, on jiyou, he was buried at Yongxi Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou in the tenth month he was buried at Yongxi Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：帝沈謀英斷，慨然有削平天下之志。

translations.literal: The encomium says: The Emperor was deep in counsel and decisive, and boldly cherished the will to level all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Taizong plotted in silence and struck without hesitation, burning with the ambition to bring the whole realm under one rule.

sentences.zh: 既即大位，陳洪進、錢俶相繼納土。

translations.literal: Once he had assumed the great position, Chen Hongjin and Qian Chu in succession surrendered their lands.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly enthroned, he watched Chen Hongjin and Qian Chu yield their domains one after another.

sentences.zh: 未幾，取太原，伐契丹，繼有交州、西夏之役。

translations.literal: Before long he took Taiyuan, campaigned against the Khitan, and in succession had campaigns in Jiaozhou and against Western Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he seized Taiyuan, marched on the Khitan, and then fought in Jiaozhou and on the Western Xia frontier.

sentences.zh: 干戈不息，天災方行，俘馘日至，而民不知兵；

translations.literal: Weapons never rested, calamities from Heaven were abroad, captives and severed heads arrived daily, yet the people did not know war;
translations.idiomatic: Arms never cooled and Heaven sent disaster after disaster, yet prisoners and trophies streamed in daily while the common folk barely felt the war;

sentences.zh: 水旱螟蝗，殆遍天下，而民不思亂。

translations.literal: flood, drought, locusts, and famine nearly covered the empire, yet the people did not think of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: floods, drought, locusts, and famine swept nearly every circuit, yet no one dreamed of revolt.

sentences.zh: 其故何也？

translations.literal: What was the reason?
translations.idiomatic: Why was this so?

sentences.zh: 帝以慈儉為寶，服濣濯之衣，毀奇巧之器，却女樂之獻，悟畋遊之非。

translations.literal: The Emperor took kindness and frugality as treasure, wore clothes of coarse floss, destroyed ingenious curiosities, refused offerings of female musicians, and understood the fault in hunting and pleasure outings.
translations.idiomatic: He treasured mercy and thrift: he wore homespun, smashed extravagant gadgets, turned away troupes of courtesans, and came to see the cost of the hunt and the pleasure park.

sentences.zh: 絕遠物，抑符瑞，閔農事，考治功。

translations.literal: He cut off distant luxuries, suppressed portents, pitied farming, and examined achievements in governance.
translations.idiomatic: He spurned exotic tribute, dismissed omens, grieved for the plow, and weighed his ministers by results.

sentences.zh: 講學以求多聞，不罪狂悖以勸諫士，哀矜惻怛，勤以自勵，日晏忘食。

translations.literal: He lectured to seek broad learning, did not punish the wild and reckless in order to encourage remonstrating scholars, was compassionate and tender-hearted, strove to admonish himself, and at late dusk forgot to eat.
translations.idiomatic: He studied to widen his knowledge, spared blunt critics to keep remonstrance alive, ruled with pity, drove himself harder each year, and often worked past supper unaware.

sentences.zh: 至於欲自焚以答天譴，欲盡除天下之賦以紓民力，卒有五兵不試、禾稼荐登之效。

translations.literal: As for wishing to burn himself to answer Heaven's punishment, or wishing to abolish all taxes under Heaven to ease the people's strength, in the end there was the effect of the five weapons unused and grain crops repeatedly ascending.
translations.idiomatic: He once spoke of offering his own body to appease Heaven and of lifting every tax to ease the people; in the end arms lay idle and the harvests piled high.

sentences.zh: 是以青、齊耆耋之叟，願率子弟治道請登禪者，接踵而至。

translations.literal: Therefore the gray-haired elders of Qing and Qi, wishing to lead sons and younger brothers to repair the roads and request the cession of the throne, arrived one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Old men in Qing and Qi lined up to mend the highways and beg him to yield the throne, their sons and grandsons in tow.

sentences.zh: 君子曰：「得乎丘民而為天子」，帝之謂乎。

translations.literal: The noble person says: "Gaining the approval of the common people and becoming Son of Heaven"—was this not the Emperor?
translations.idiomatic: As Mencius said, to win the common people is to become Son of Heaven—and that was Taizong.

sentences.zh: 故帝之功德，炳煥史牒，號稱賢君。

translations.literal: Thus the Emperor's merit and virtue shine brilliantly in the historical registers, and he is called a worthy ruler.
translations.idiomatic: So his merit blazes from the annals and posterity calls him a sage king.

sentences.zh: 若夫太祖之崩不逾年而改元，涪陵縣公之貶死，武功王之自殺，宋后之不成喪，則後世不能無議焉。

translations.literal: As for the Founding Ancestor's death and the change of reign title within a year, the demotion and death of the Duke of Fuling, the Prince of Wugong's suicide, and Empress Song's incomplete mourning—on these later ages cannot be without debate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the hasty era change within a year of Taizu's death, the ruin of the Prince of Fuling, the suicide of the Prince of Wugong, and the curtailed mourning for Empress Song have given later critics ample grounds for doubt.
